reviews.text: A fun incremental game where you harvest crops for a gluttonous King. There are cool combinations between crops, weapons, and skills. No missable achievements, 100% = ~4h. [b]Approximate time to 100%:[/b] 4 [b]Estimated achievement difficulty:[/b] 1/10 [b]Minimum number of playthroughs needed:[/b] 1 [b]Is there a good guide available:[/b] You don't need a guide [b]Multiplayer achievements:[/b] No [b]Missable achievements:[/b] No [b]Grinding Achievements:[/b] No [b]DLC-Only achievements:[/b] No [b]Speedrun achievements:[/b] No [b]Time-gated achievements:[/b] No [b]RNG-achievements:[/b] No [b]Does difficulty affect achievements:[/b] No difficulty option [b]Unobtainable/glitched achievements:[/b] No [b]Gamepad or mouse and keyboard:[/b] Definitely mouse Agrivore: Incremental Farming is a satisfying incremental game in which you harvest crops to feed the gluttonous King. You start with one simple crop, one weapon, and one skill. However, you can unlock a bunch more, and those will allow some crazy combos that just feel good. Very early on, I loved the Garlic crop, as it allows you to spawn bats that circle around you and do damage to crops. Later on, I loved the mushrooms as they let you start each round with gold crops, which was very nice in combination with the bow or the laser beams' special ability. Your starting farm has only the option for one crop, one weapon, and one skill, but later farms allow for more crops and more skills, so you can make even crazier combos! Your meta progress comes from unlocking the skill tree in the current run, and the amount of red diamonds you get is also determined by which farm you are playing. However, on the later farms, you can select more crops, which will make the skill tree bigger, but if you just want to quickly grind meta progression, it might even be better to not go for the extra crops as you still get the maximum amount of red diamonds when completing the skill tree, but this way the skill tree is not so big. Another thing to keep in mind is which skill you choose first, as that will determine which skill you will unlock first in the skill tree of that run. Just a small thing, but it can have a big impact on how smoothly the start goes. The only thing I struggled with was finding the skills in the skill tree that aren't fully unlocked yet. It became a bit of a "Where is Wally/Waldo?" game from time to time. The completed skills have a green border at this moment; the incomplete ones are grey/white and have a + symbol in their picture. This is quite hard to find in a sea of bright colors. However, I know the developer is looking into this after I told him my struggles with sometimes finding that one skill I hadn't fully upgraded. Agrivore: Incremental Farming has no missable achievements and can be completed in around 4 hours. I give Agrivore: Incremental Farming 4 out of 5 stars. 全成就了20多部点击增量类游戏了,多少算是对这个品类有点理解. 先提供最简单的策略退化玩法: 无论什么阶段 点出满级蘑菇并作为首选,再随意带其他作物,前期用满级弓后期用满级激光,都可以在3倍速,4分钟内完成一次轮回喵 可以给出结论:本作是我迄今为止玩过的最差同品类游戏. 0/10 优点:游戏内置3倍速 没了. 剩下的都是难以容忍的缺点 1.除弓外全武器存在攻击碰撞检测BUG. 新玩家在点出剑的右键技能时就应该能感受到:在技能持续时间内,攻击几乎只能命中1-2个目标.霰弹枪和激光实际上也存在该BUG,但感知不明显. 2.单局(下称轮回)加点策略僵化 无论选择什么BD,加点思路均相同,先点出最近植物的2个加钱,然后点出提高作物概率和主武器伤害,接下来的加点也根据 收入→概率→附加效果 来依次点出即可. 这一点也同时导致本作的核心玩法 极度 无趣,在选择弓和激光时纯当做挂机游戏来玩,只是几秒钟就要重开一局徒增操作量罢了. 3.局外成长仅是拖游戏时长的工具. 点出轮回内的全部升级,视为完成单局,玩家可以得到3/5/7个点数,用于点局外成长的技能树,但技能树只用于开启一些新的同质化的内容,换了个SPRITE的静态作物,换了个SPRITE多了几个投射物的霰弹枪,玩到现在解锁的十几个东西里面,只有 弓箭 和 激光 还有 农业无人机 算是眼前一亮,其他的设计都非常无趣.且由于接下来提到的第4点,甚至会导致你新点出的内容反而让你的下一次轮回体验更加差劲. 4.灾难性的数值平衡. 或许你会认为开启新作物/武器/工具能让你的下一次轮回更加轻松,但并非如此 先说作物: 有一个没写出来的机制:本作的作物越强(单株收入越高),其对应的技能树所需的金币数越高,且为指数级上升. 在高阶段(每个阶段可以带的作物总数+1)时,阶段本身就会给高阶作物价格一个乘数 这两点这导致了什么问题?——带前期农作物反而能更舒适更快速的玩成一次轮回,高阶作物卡钱卡到怀疑人生 最优选是 满级蘑菇-满级土豆-任意 全金+全刷新+低价 再说武器: 激光之前, 弓箭 是唯一有用的武器,因为这是唯一一个判定区没有BUG的武器...弓箭开右键=清屏,其他武器开右键说不定反而降低DPS(因为攻击判定的BUG). 二阶段解锁的三把枪被视为三种武器(他们实际上都是指向一个区域的霰弹枪,只不过越后面的单次射击子弹越多),要知道想完成全成就需要用所有BD通关一次,这也代表着要被这个B枪折磨三个轮回. 激光想用的话至少点到2级,1级的情况仍会被判定BUG折磨 5.其他琐碎问题 中文翻译错误极多,建议找个好点的AI重新跑一下 建议提供一键加满单技能/一键分配自动加满的功能,后期点技能耗时比游玩时间还多.. 割草近乎0反馈,没有声效/震动/动画/跳钱动效...什么也没有 总结如下,个人认为本作丢失了点击增量类游戏所有的魅力 1.没有庞大养成树所带来的数值成长乐趣 2.不存在此类游戏常见的,点出技能树中某个新机制后质变游戏体验的内容 3.游戏过程中,能提供新鲜感的地方,个人认为只有初次使用弓箭/初次使用激光,没了 4.由于过低的操作需求(参考咖啡星的集环/龟龟前中期的氧气和右键资源管理),玩家实际上的GAMEPLAY只有两件事:核心玩法部分开3倍速挂机不动→拿到的钱去点一模一样的技能树.机械式的重复劳动这一块! 最终本作的游戏循环,就是在一个简陋的画面里,重复一次又一次的挂机操作(笑点解析-玩弓箭和激光外的武器还不能美美挂机),重复同样的顺序升级同样的技能树,在不了解策略退化的情况下,还要被逆天的数值和BUG折磨 无趣.
很爽的增量游戏，2.5小时拿下全成就。 如果你想爽的话，一阶段无脑蘑菇，二阶段无脑玉米，三阶段无脑黑洞。 武器二阶段加农炮无敌，三阶段激光只要别忘了按右键就行。 升级前期直接冲蘑菇的8秒增产，然后点蘑菇金币，直接五六分钟一张图。无人机星尘工具三阶段过度最快。 到了四阶段无脑拿升级点就行，把前面没升满的全升满了。 感觉第一次熟悉2.5小时全成就通关，差一点能退款GTMD。
头一回见一款增量游戏一大半的时间都是在点天赋树，而且是非常频繁，手指都点废了，数值也是用脚填，除了折磨感觉不到任何爽感

反馈：没有demo好玩，我正是因为demo极致的爽感才添加的愿望单，结果正式版的游戏玩法和demo居然天差地别，游戏流程枯燥乏味完全失去了割草爽游的所有优点。 建议：个人建议，游戏里面可以设置两个游戏模式，第一个模式就是正式版这个不断献祭农场的玩法，第二个模式就是demo版里面的无尽模式，至于两个模式之间是否需要有所联系就看制作组自己的想法了，但是我倾向于两种游戏模式完全可以独立互不干扰，当然可以将成就均匀分配在两种游戏模式中，这对热衷于收集全成就的玩家而言也会更有动力去体验整个游戏。 PS：鉴于目前的游戏体验，我并不推荐这款标榜着“割草爽游”的天赋树点击游戏，希望制作组可以认真考虑我的建议，谢谢。

Agrivore, developed by verty and published by Rogue Duck Interactive and Gamersky Games, is an incremental roguelite that blends idle progression with active, moment-to-moment input in a way that feels immediately approachable yet quietly system-driven beneath the surface. It takes the familiar satisfaction loop of idle games—numbers growing, upgrades stacking, efficiency improving—and injects it with just enough interactivity to keep the player engaged rather than passive. The setup is intentionally minimal. You are placed in a role where your primary goal is to harvest crops and generate output for an ever-demanding authority figure, but this framing exists mostly to support the mechanics rather than drive a narrative. The game does not attempt to build a story or emotional arc; instead, it leans entirely on its gameplay loop to carry the experience. This stripped-down approach works in its favor, as it keeps the focus tightly on progression, optimization, and experimentation. Gameplay revolves around moving your character through fields of crops that continuously spawn and fill the screen. Harvesting is largely automatic, but positioning and movement determine how efficiently you gather resources. This creates a subtle layer of skill, as players can influence the speed and effectiveness of their runs through active play. At the same time, the incremental nature of the game ensures that progress is always being made, even when actions are minimal. The combination of these elements gives the game a hybrid identity, sitting somewhere between a fully idle experience and a lightweight action system. A significant part of the game’s appeal comes from its build variety. Players can equip different tools, crops, and modifiers that interact with each other in ways that can dramatically change how a run unfolds. Some combinations create chain reactions that rapidly increase output, while others focus on steady, consistent growth. Discovering and refining these synergies becomes the central form of engagement, as players experiment with different setups to find the most efficient approach. The inclusion of a persistent upgrade system further enhances this, allowing progress to carry over between runs and gradually expanding the range of possible strategies. The structure is built around repeated sessions, each contributing to overall advancement. Runs are short and self-contained, making it easy to play in brief bursts while still feeling a sense of progression. Over time, the game introduces more options and complexity, encouraging players to think more carefully about their choices. However, the core loop remains largely unchanged, and while the numbers grow and the builds evolve, the fundamental actions stay consistent. Visually, Agrivore adopts a clean and colorful style that prioritizes readability. The screen can become crowded with crops and effects, but the design ensures that important elements remain clear. This is essential for a game where efficiency depends on quickly understanding what is happening at any given moment. The overall presentation is simple but cohesive, supporting the gameplay without adding unnecessary distractions. The audio design follows a similar approach, providing subtle feedback and background music that complements the pace without becoming intrusive. One of the game’s strengths is its pacing. It strikes a balance between being relaxing and engaging, allowing players to choose how actively they want to participate. It works well as a short-session experience, offering quick bursts of progress that feel rewarding without requiring a long-term commitment. At the same time, players who want to dive deeper into optimization can spend more time refining their builds and experimenting with different strategies. However, the simplicity of the core loop also leads to its main limitation. While the build system adds variety, the overall structure does not change significantly as the game progresses. This can make extended play sessions feel repetitive, particularly once players have identified effective strategies. The relatively limited scope of content also means that the experience may feel complete sooner than expected, especially for those who quickly grasp its systems. Ultimately, Agrivore succeeds in delivering a focused and satisfying incremental experience with just enough interactivity to stand out from more passive titles. It does not aim to be expansive or deeply complex, but it offers a polished loop of growth and experimentation that is easy to engage with and consistently rewarding within its scope. In the end, it stands as a compact and enjoyable game that blends idle mechanics with active play in a way that feels natural and engaging. While it may not sustain long-term interest for every player, it provides a solid and well-executed experience for those who appreciate incremental progression with a touch of strategy. Rating: 7/10

Interesting take on the incremental genre. Looks nice, plays fast, makes you spend money on tech tree and repeat. Once you reach a certain limit, you reset your farm, spend your gems on upgrades and go again. I will give thumbs up since it's pretty cheap and it's fun for a couple of hours, but it does not scale well. The crops come in with their tech-tree abilities and mushroom's ability allows it to scale really fast. Eventually you end up using the same formula over and over again. But for a couple of bucks it wouldn't be fair to expect a 10+ hours gameplay I guess. The foundation is pretty good though so if the dev could come up with a more interesting mid-end game it would be even better.

已经通关了。说实话有点短，而且其中有时候开新的区域需要刷宝石（也有可能是作者想让玩家尝试更多构筑）。 下面说说我的感受。 游戏本体方面：游戏玩的时候有时候会在收割画面卡住（大概半秒），疑似优化的问题，虽然整体不错，但是在收割的时候卡住很影响体验。 游戏内容方面： 1.武器系统 a.好像可以通过来回刷进行升级（每一局的技能树的升级），不知道是我的错觉还是什么，建议游戏增加说明； b.武器我感觉前期好用的是剑，中期是种田大师，后期M61作物风暴。武器和武器之间差距还是挺大的，尤其是初始攻击力方面差距有点大。钢剑和M61作物风暴初始攻击力差很多，在后期不得不选择初始攻击力更高的武器才能获得比较好的体验，否则就是折磨。 2.作物系统 a.我个人观点最好用的不是最贵的，而是蘑菇。蘑菇的buff非常强力，尤其是把buff时间和收益都加满以后，赚钱非常快，如果多作物的情况下，配合其它高价值作物，基本上10-15次收割就结束。 b.其它的作物区别不大，只不过越后来的作物技能树价格贵很多，没有蘑菇的配合打起来发展很慢。 3.技能系统 各有各的好，除了最开始的光照。 4.罪孽 各有各的好 希望后续更新能再增加一些内容。

Love the game, but I’m still leaving a negative review because there are a few major issues that dragged the experience down for me. [spoiler]Beat the game in 2.6 hours with all upgrades unlocked.[/spoiler] 1. Seed selection feels broken. Garlic was almost always the first crop regardless of order/randomness, sometimes the crop order was random and sometimes not, feels broken to me. 2. [spoiler]Mushrooms[/spoiler] are massively overpowered. There’s basically no reason to use anything else for most of the game. The king’s mood system doesn’t really solve this either — it just forces you off [spoiler]mushrooms[/spoiler] every few rounds instead of making other crops actually competitive. Right now [spoiler]dark matter/mushrooms and corn[/spoiler] completely overshadow almost everything else. 3. There’s very little incentive to experiment with other weapons, even though the weapons themselves are designed well. 4. Greenhouse upgrades seem bugged: * Harvest interval goes UP instead of DOWN with upgrades. * The “highest value crop” upgrade doesn’t seem to work, greenhouses still give random crops anyway. 5. [spoiler]Corn[/spoiler] seems inconsistent or broken: * It either doesn’t pop correctly or doesn’t apply the yield multiplier. * [spoiler]Gemini lasers[/spoiler] also don’t seem to trigger the multiplier properly. 6. Audio design needs work. A lot of sounds are extremely sharp/high-pitched and genuinely uncomfortable with headphones or speakers. The upgrade hover sound especially sounds like my speakers are breaking, and the purchase sound is painfully pointy. I ended up muting SFX entirely. 7. “Buy cheapest node” becomes a clicker simulator in late game. Needs something like: * Buy max cheapest nodes * Hold-to-buy * Auto-purchase option 8. [spoiler]Stardust[/spoiler] skill tooltip in the treasury is incorrect. 9. “Buy cheapest node” overlaps UI elements in the skill tree menu (probably the [spoiler]sin[/spoiler] tooltip). That said, core gameplay loop is nice, the game just needs balancing and polish.

I'm kind of on the fence about the game, and that's why I'm not recommending it. It's very simple and enjoyable, but there are a few QoL updates that it needs. The most frustrating thing is that they put in the "King's Mood" update, which is designed to add a little randomness to runs by trying to create a disincentive against spamming the same crop pattern. I like that in concept, but the problem is that the balance of the crops and weapons is not good. I would love for them to be rebalanced. Maybe additional skills or something? Or have the other trees have upgrades for them so they're progress locked. But like, if I like the Bow, having an upgrade in a future that puts on extra bows, or give me extra swords so I have a sword blender by the end of the game. just. there's no reason to keep using it as I progress in the game. I think the laser weapon may be bugged, and the game doesn't inform you what Skills, weapons or crops do. You have to just invest in them, try it and hope you like it or you're going to be stuck with that for the run. The crops are also not very well balanced. The top tier crops (Starfruit and Darkfruit) cost an excessive amount, to the point that if you don't use mushrooms, it's just not worth trying to max them out each run because it required millions of gold per upgrade level. The only thing that ramps up that fast was Mushroom Boost, which gives a multiplier to harvest for the crops. It's disappointing that early crops, especially wheat, are basically useless in Mid- to Late-Game. I still don't really know what Darkfruit does, beyond having some sort of gravity-style effect. It's just... yeah. It needs a bit more work in the game. It's fun, and short, and I don't regret playing it. BUT! It just has improvements it needs to get it over that hump, if that makes sense.

Agrivore: Incremental Farming is a poor incremental games. At a glance it did look good, but I couldn't have been further from the truth. In 3 hours that it took to beat the game, I've forgotten how many gripes and bugs I've found, but I'll do my best to recall all of them... As far as bug goes, sometimes I've had the gameplay loop on top of the 'results' screen... a few time I was about to buy some upgrades in the upgrade screen and the gameplay just started IN THE UPDATE SCREEN, without the farm's background. Wow. Aside from that, some weapon graphics are totally broken (the gun skill one and probably others as well). As far as bad decisions go: Why are the runs like 15 seconds each until the very end of the game??? Why do crops that gives more money have skill trees that cost more money to unlock, in the end... they're just not really any better? The 2x and 3x speed options in the menu doesn't help, the rounds last 10 and 5 seconds approximately with it enabled! Oh and the worst for last: Why in the world would you NERF THE PLAYERS FAVORITE CROPS? If you constantly pick your favorite crop when building your skill tree/farms, the crops take 50% longer to kill and you start with only 2 of the max instead of 5-6... Building a skill tree is kind of fun and the game could've enjoyable but it's not polished at all and it suffers from insane balancing issues and lack of clarity. I don't know what anything I'm unlocking in the prestige tree do, the money the crop gives is not shown, the damage of the weapon isn't shown, I bought 3 different crops in my first reset because I wanted to get a bunch of crops, turns out you're limited to one of them for the first few resets and you can't refund your prestige upgrades, so I practically prestiged and started over for nothing. I unlocked some prestige upgrade that nerfs later synergies with them, can't reset them. I unlocked a final prestige tree with the final farm unlock and I beat the boss after 4 rounds because the game isn't balanced, didn't get to try any of the sins upgrades... Overall, a buggy, unpolished and quirky letdown of a game.
